eligibilityData.eligibilityBasisNote: No eligibility conclusion is asserted. Whether the programme was satisfactorily completed, whether the conditions of probation were complied with, and whether any subsection (f) bar applies are the participant's own statements of fact, each checked by the participant against a document they obtain. Whether the prosecuting attorney objects, and how the court finds on any alleged probation violation, are never predicted.
eligibilityData.supportingDocumentNote: Every document named here is participant-obtained. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect any of them, and no drafted document characterises what any of them says.
additionalFacts: Timeline prepared for the Petitioner's petition under W. Va. Code § 17C-5-2b(g).
10/01/2023 — charges dismissed. The one-year period runs from this date and expired on 10/01/2024.
As of the filing date the statutory waiting period is satisfied and the Petitioner is eligible.
The probation office confirmed to LegalEase that probation expired on 09/09/2023 and that no violation occurred.
The record was sealed and destroyed on 02/01/2026 following the Court's order, and the acquittal is now complete.

partyDataFieldNote: partyData uses the PleadingRenderInput field names petitionerName / petitionerAddress / otherNamesUsed. The role label is set by presentation.movantRole in the config, not by the fixture key name; the word petitioner is prohibited in rendered output.
identityFieldNote: caseData.docketNumber holds the participant's own case number and caseData.countyName their own county; both are required screening answers and are deliberately left blank in the fixtures under the artifact convention. The rendered document cannot go out without them; they are supplied by the participant, never by LegalEase. caseData.court is left blank because no source read for this track states the court level — the compiled profile records West Virginia courts as circuit, magistrate or municipal.
expectFailure: Must fail pleading QA. (1) Prohibited terms: 'petition', 'Petitioner', 'sealed', 'destroyed' and 'acquittal'. (2) It computes the one-year period and states it as satisfied, and it computes it from the WRONG date — the dismissal rather than the expiration of the term of probation, which is exactly the error the registry's packet instruction exists to prevent. The timeline states dates; it does not compute, conclude or assert eligibility. (3) It asserts an outside-party act no source states: that the probation office confirmed the expiry date and the absence of violations directly to LegalEase. LegalEase does not obtain, receive or inspect any of the four participant documents. (4) It asserts a court act and a completed records outcome — an order, a sealing and a destruction — none of which any source states and none of which this route may predict. (5) It proceeds while priorFelonyConviction reports a felony conviction, which bars the subsection (g) motion outright, and while probationViolations reports alleged repeated violations. (a) It fills court identity no source supplies: a circuit-court name, a county, a case number, an OTN, a judge, a prosecutor and a filing date, none of which LegalEase may prefill — the compiled profile records West Virginia courts as circuit, magistrate or municipal and no source read for this track says which hears a § 17C-5-2b matter. (b) It populates protected fields — date of birth, SSN last four, state ID, driver's licence number, FBI number and a fingerprint identifier — which must stay blank. (c) It asserts outside-party acts no source states: that the Division of Motor Vehicles confirmed completion directly to LegalEase, and that the prosecuting attorney was served and does not object. Service is the participant's own act, attested by the participant, and no prosecutor position is ever stated. (d) It asserts a hearing outcome and predicts that the court will grant. (e) It states an eligibilityBasisLabel asserting confirmed eligibility when no eligibility conclusion may be asserted on this track. (f) It states a fee amount and a waiver: § 17C-5-2b charges no fee for either motion, subsection (h) court costs are stated nowhere as an amount, the registry records the fee waiver as 'none stated in § 17C-5-2b', and the $100 State Police processing fee belongs to the § 61-11-26 conviction route.
